content:
Since the iPhone 4 launched with a bumper case, bumper cases have remained popular, but truly good options are scarce. Rhinoshield offers a solid choice for users who prefer a minimalist style.

Apple finally returned to the bumper case market last year, releasing a bumper case for the iPhone Air. Some had hoped Apple would extend its bumper case line to the iPhone 18 Pro (just as it once released a clear case for the iPhone 11), but that unfortunately never materialised. While searching for an alternative, I came across Rhinoshield's Minimalist Impact Bumper.

Key details

The fit of the Impact Bumper is much like a typical bumper case, with a low lip around the screen edge but a slightly raised back. One particularly clever design feature I appreciate is the support structure, which prevents the camera plateau and lenses from making direct contact with the surface the phone is placed on—something especially useful for the aluminium-bodied 17 Pro and 18 Pro. This offers better protection than most bumper cases and also solves the awkward wobble when the phone lies flat on a table.

However, the fit is not quite as snug as I'd like. Once installed, it feels a little loose, and the edges are prone to prying outward, making me worry about warping over time. That said, I'm confident the phone won't easily pop out of the case upon impact (I've accidentally tested this). The case is made of hard plastic rather than rubber, so hopefully it holds up over the long run. Rhinoshield says the product is made from a single material and is 100% recyclable.

There are currently three colour options, all designed to complement the iPhone 18 Pro body colours: white, blue and black (those hoping for burgundy will be disappointed). I chose the blue, which is close to Glacier but not exactly the same.

Downsides

The case does have its drawbacks. My biggest complaint is that the buttons are extremely difficult to press. For some reason, they went with an almost flush design, and combined with the button structure, they feel mushy and unsatisfying to press.

The overall material choice can also be considered a drawback. To me, the feel doesn't match the bumper case for the iPhone Air, though some may actually prefer this texture. Personally, I find it more tolerable than typical TPU/rubber clear case materials. However, this material, paired with the looser fit, seems particularly prone to picking up lint from pockets.

If you use Apple's Wrist Strap or Crossbody Strap, note that this case does not provide any attachment points for them.

Wrapping up

Rhinoshield's bumper case is far from perfect, and I still wish Apple would extend its bumper case line to other iPhone models. In the end, I decided to keep this case for one simple reason: it offers me a near caseless experience without having to worry about the aluminium body getting scratched or dented. As far as I know, this bumper case is typically only sold on their own website, priced at around $30, which with shipping comes close to Apple's $39 price tag. You can purchase the Rhinoshield Minimalist Impact Bumper here. (It occasionally shows up on Amazon, so keep an eye out.)
